description.value: The study examined whether FTLD-TDP type, GRN mutation status, and FTLD-MND status are associated with distinct patterns of brain atrophy using voxel-based morphometry of volumetric MRI.
In this case-control study, subjects with pathologically confirmed FTLD-TDP and volumetric MRI were compared with age- and gender-matched normal controls.

spans.text: Atlas-based parcellation showed greater lateral temporal atrophy in GRN-positive subjects than GRN-negative subjects (p = 0.007), with no significant difference observed in frontal and parietal regions (figure 2).
those with mutations in GRN showed significantly greater loss in the lateral temporal lobe than those without mutations
A VBM direct comparison showed greater involvement of temporal and parietal lobes in GRN-positive subjects compared to GRN-negative subjects at an uncorrected threshold of p < 0.001

value: The type 1 subjects with and without mutations in GRN both showed gray matter loss in frontal, temporal, and parietal lobes compared to controls. Those with mutations in GRN showed significantly greater loss in the lateral temporal lobe than those without mutations.

value: Type 1 and type 3 subjects with FTLD-MND showed almost identical patterns of gray matter loss involving posterior frontal lobes bilaterally compared to controls. The findings suggest that patterns of atrophy may not solely be driven by FTLD-TDP type, but that the pathology of FTLD-MND may have a signature.

spans.text: Type 1 and type 3 subjects with FTLD-MND showed almost identical patterns of gray matter loss involving posterior frontal lobes bilaterally compared to controls.
